answer: A trust-flow network limits Sybil attacks by restricting agent interactions to capacity-bounded credit channels. Because honest nodes refuse to harbor unbacked links, an attacker must lock scarce financial capital across each trust ridge to connect forged peers to the wider economy. This imposes real balance-sheet expenditure per spawned identity. However, this design causes liquidity fragmentation, stranding legitimate agents on a multi-hop transactional voyage across disconnected clusters.
